subject: Capacity uplift: segmented buckets + lock-in pricing request
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie@nimbushealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on adding capacity mid-contract

Hi Priyom,

Hope you're well — quick one from our side. We had a Q2 spike in inference usage for our triage models and are going to need ~35% more capacity for the next 6 months. Our renewal isn't until Jan 2028, so this would be a mid-contract top-up.

Before I bring procurement in, can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood supports segmented top-ups (we'd like to carve this into a separate bucket for analytics), 2) if there are short-term commitment discounts available, and 3) how pricing behaves if we later annualize this into our Jan renewal (co-term).

Appreciate any quick guidance — happy to jump on a 20-minute call.

Thanks,
Julie Park
Head of ML Ops, Nimbus Health
julie@nimbushealth.com

P.S. Procurement asked we surface any potential PO path early so they can align on timelines.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on adding capacity mid-contract

Hi Julie — thanks for the note and congrats on the Q2 lift. Short answers up front: yes (segmented buckets), yes (short-term uplift discounts possible), and we can provide clear annualization paths for Jan renewal with a co-term conversion.

I attached three pragmatic options (pricing-options.xlsx) — TL;DR:
- Option A (Bridge voucher): immediate bucket add, 6-month voucher at 12% off list; preserves your Jan renewal rate baseline if annualized.
- Option B (Temporary committed tier): commit for 6 months at lower unit rate but requires one-time partial prepayment; converts to co-term at a pre-agreed uplift factor.
- Option C (Burst credits): pay-as-you-go credits with marginally higher unit price, no long-term commitment.

Thoughts on next steps: if you want the Bridge voucher we can draft a brief amendment and finance can issue an interim invoice; procurement typically needs the amendment + PO. If you'd prefer to annualize now we can model the blended price into Jan and show the delta.

I copied Marissa (Sales Ops) to confirm discount guardrails and Grace (CS) for onboarding impact. If procurement needs a PO template I can attach a draft.

Would you be available for a 20-min sync Monday morning?

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0138

Attachment: pricing-options.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 sheets)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Nimbus uplift options (for Priyom)

Priyom — reviewed Julie's ask and your options. Notes from Sales Ops / Finance:

- Bridge voucher (Option A) is viable; recommended discount cap at 12% for a 6-month voucher to avoid downstream revenue recognition issues.
- For Option B (temporary committed tier) Finance wants a minimal prepayment of 30% of the uplift notional to secure capacity. That allows us to reserve GPUs on Dedicated pools.
- Option C is fine for pure consumption but will likely cost them ~18% more versus A over a 6-month run at their predicted usage.

Operational ask from CS (Grace): we need 2 weeks lead time to provision segmented buckets + prefix caching, so communicate that to the customer before the PO.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

2) Can you include explicit language that the voucher will convert to our Jan 2028 renewal at the baseline rate (no retroactive price increases) if we choose to annualize?

I'll have Procurement attach a PO draft — attaching a placeholder now (PO-Nimbus-Health.pdf) so you can see the format. If you can send the amendment + a 7-day hold on the pricing we can move quickly.
